reel: 1969: the US Army Corps of Engineers turned off the American Falls at Niagara
status: 7 photos downloaded and viewed. Three COLOUR 1969 photos of the dewatered falls come from the US Army Corps of Engineers Buffalo District's own 50th-anniversary release on DVIDS (marked PUBLIC DOMAIN by DVIDS/USACE; captions credit the original photographer as W. Stratton of the Niagara Frontier State Park Commission). Two Wikimedia Commons 1969 photos (one CC BY-SA 4.0 B&W, one PD colour but only 618 px) and two 1973 DOCUMERICA colour aerials (NARA, PD) for the 'water on' comparison. SHA1 of every Commons download matches the Commons API. No rights-clear film of the dry falls found. The 1974 American Falls International Board report (DTIC ADA101298) could not be downloaded: apps.dtic.mil was returning an 'Under Maintenance' page on 2026-11-02, so no report figures/diagrams are included.

assets.license: Public domain (DVIDS 'PUBLIC DOMAIN' release by US Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District; VIRIN 190611-A-YS819-003; original 1520x1052)
assets.license_note: DVIDS/USACE publish this as public domain, but the caption credits the 1969 photographer as 'W. Stratton of the Niagara Frontier State Park Commission' (a New York State body), so it is not strictly a federal work. Low-to-moderate risk; keep the Corps + Stratton credit line.
assets.credit_line: Photo: W. Stratton, Niagara Frontier State Park Commission, via U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Buffalo District (DVIDS, public domain)
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR, 1969. The dewatered American Falls from Prospect Point: a dry rock lip with one thin trickle of water, a huge pile of green-tinged talus boulders below, the Niagara gorge at left, the Prospect Point observation tower and Rainbow Bridge behind. Faded 1960s print with a cream border.
assets.best_segments: OPENER. Crop the cream border off (image area is about x 70-1880, y 70-1270). 9:16 crop centred on the trickle + tower (x about 560-1310) or a slow push from the Rainbow Bridge down to the talus. Pairs with americanfalls_1973_aerial_documerica.jpg (same tower, water on).

assets.license: Public domain (DVIDS 'PUBLIC DOMAIN' release by US Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District; VIRIN 190612-A-YS819-005; original 3507x2480)
assets.license_note: Same caveat as above: credited to W. Stratton of the Niagara Frontier State Park Commission; published by the Corps as public domain. The 3507 px original needs a DVIDS login; this is the 2000 px public rendition.
assets.credit_line: Photo: W. Stratton, Niagara Frontier State Park Commission, via U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Buffalo District (DVIDS, public domain)
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR aerial, 1969 (bare trees, so autumn). The whole dewatered American Falls crest and the empty, pale riverbed of the American Rapids above it, the talus pile at the foot, the Niagara Falls NY skyline (United Office Building) and the river upstream. Taken from above the Canadian side.
assets.best_segments: The 'turned off' reveal: pan along the dry crest (y about 760-900) then tilt down to the talus. Also the best image for showing how big the talus pile is relative to the cliff.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR, 1969, from river level on the Canadian side: the full dry face of the American Falls with two small remaining trickles (Bridal Veil at left, a leak at centre), the talus boulder slope reaching halfway up the cliff, brown river in the foreground. Cream print border.
assets.best_segments: The 'talus' beat (rock pile halfway up the face). Crop the border (image area about x 70-1870, y 70-1250). Zoom on the boulders at centre for the 'study the rock' line.

assets.what_it_shows: BLACK AND WHITE, July 1969, from the Canadian side: the dry American Falls face with a thin trickle, the talus pile, Rainbow Bridge at far left, the Niagara Falls NY skyline (United Office Building, Hotel Niagara) behind. Scratched negative scan, very high resolution.
assets.best_segments: Best resolution of the set: use for the big slow push-in on the dry cliff and trickle (x about 1800-3700). Good second shot after the colour opener; B&W reads as 'archive'.
